title: Categorical equivalences of labelled coproducts of quasicategories
statement:
Use small simplicial sets and quasicategories as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] and categorical equivalences as in [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure], in its fixed universe. Let $I$ be a small set, let $X_i,Y_i$ be small quasicategories for each $i\in I$, and let $f_i:X_i\to Y_i$ be simplicial maps. Form the degreewise disjoint unions $X=\coprod_{i\in I}X_i$ and $Y=\coprod_{i\in I}Y_i$, with all simplicial operators preserving the index $i$. They are quasicategories, and the label-preserving map
$$f=\coprod_{i\in I}f_i:X\longrightarrow Y$$
is a categorical equivalence if and only if every $f_i$ is a categorical equivalence. Empty $I$ and empty individual quasicategories are permitted; no connectedness of $X_i$ or $Y_i$ is assumed.

source.place: Proof of Theorem B.0.20, edge-pullback accessibility argument; auxiliary labelled-coproduct comparison extracted from the retained proof using the quasi-inverse characterization of categorical equivalences. Agent-derived helper, not a named theorem asserted to occur in HA; no Stacks tag states this comparison.

proof.text: In the degreewise coproduct, every face and degeneracy preserves the label. In particular all vertices of a simplex have its label, and an edge cannot join different labels. Every inner horn has a connected edge graph: for $n=2$ it is the two-edge spine, and for $n\geq3$ it contains every edge of $\Delta^n$. Thus a map $\Lambda_k^n\to X$ has all vertices in one $X_i$; every simplex of the horn then has that same label, so the entire map factors through $X_i$. Fill it there and include the filler in $X$. This proves that $X$ is a quasicategory; the identical argument proves it for $Y$. If a coproduct is empty there is no map from an inner horn into it, so its horn condition is vacuous. The degreewise coproducts are small because the index set and all summands are small in the fixed universe.

source.place: Agent-written horn argument from the simplicial and inner-horn definitions; compare the quasicategory convention used in section 3.6.

proof.text: Suppose each $f_i$ is a categorical equivalence. Clause (2) of [lem-coef-joyal-quasicategory-characterizations] supplies a simplicial map $g_i:Y_i\to X_i$ and equivalence edges $\alpha_i:g_if_i\to\operatorname{id}_{X_i}$ and $\beta_i:f_ig_i\to\operatorname{id}_{Y_i}$ in the corresponding functor simplicial sets. Choose these data for the small family. Include, for each equivalence edge, its inverse edge and the two $2$-simplices witnessing the inverse equations, as specified in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. These witnesses are maps $X_i\times\Delta^r\to X_i$ or $Y_i\times\Delta^r\to Y_i$, with $r=1,2$, whose face equations are the inverse equations.

source.place: Remark 3.6.5, Corollary 3.6.6 and Theorem 3.6.8, printed pp.114-116; specialization of the existing quasi-inverse characterization.

proof.text: Set $g(i,y)=(i,g_i(y))$ in every simplicial degree. Simplicial operators preserve $i$, so this defines $g:Y\to X$. For every $r$, the degreewise bijection $X\times\Delta^r=\coprod_i(X_i\times\Delta^r)$ sends $((i,x),t)$ to $(i,(x,t))$ and commutes with every simplicial operator. Assemble the maps for $\alpha_i$, their inverses and both triangular witnesses by this bijection and the coproduct inclusions. Every face equation holds on each summand and therefore on the coproduct. They give an equivalence edge $gf\to\operatorname{id}_X$ in $\operatorname{Fun}(X,X)$. The same construction gives $fg\to\operatorname{id}_Y$ in $\operatorname{Fun}(Y,Y)$, retaining its inverse and both triangle witnesses. Step 1 supplies the quasicategory hypotheses, so clause (2) of [lem-coef-joyal-quasicategory-characterizations] proves that $f$ is a categorical equivalence.

source.place: Agent-written assembly of simplicial quasi-inverse data, using Corollary 3.6.6 and Theorem 3.6.8, printed pp.114-116.

proof.text: Conversely suppose $f$ is a categorical equivalence. By step 1 and clause (2) of [lem-coef-joyal-quasicategory-characterizations], choose a simplicial quasi-inverse $g:Y\to X$ and equivalence edges $\alpha:gf\to\operatorname{id}_X$, $\beta:fg\to\operatorname{id}_Y$, with inverse edges and both inverse triangles. At a vertex $y\in Y_i$, evaluation of $\beta$ gives an edge from $f(g(y))$ to $y$ in $Y$. Its endpoints have the same label, namely $i$. Since $f$ preserves labels, $g(y)$ has label $i$. For any simplex $s$ of $Y_i$, a vertex of $g(s)$ is $g$ of a vertex of $s$, hence has label $i$; the whole simplex $g(s)$ consequently lies in $X_i$. Thus $g$ restricts to a simplicial map $g_i:Y_i\to X_i$, and compatibility with faces and degeneracies follows from that of $g$. This argument uses no connectedness of $Y_i$.

source.place: Agent-written label restriction of the quasi-inverse supplied by Corollary 3.6.6 and Theorem 3.6.8, printed pp.114-116.

proof.text: Restrict the maps defining $\alpha$, its inverse and the two inverse triangles to $X_i\times\Delta^r$, for $r=1,2$. Each vertex of each such domain is sent into $X_i$: the functors at the vertices of the parameter simplex are $gf$ or $\operatorname{id}_X$, whose restrictions both preserve label $i$ by step 4. Every simplex of the domain has a vertex, and its image has the label of that vertex, so each restricted map factors through $X_i$. The restricted face equations are unchanged, giving an equivalence edge $g_if_i\to\operatorname{id}_{X_i}$ in $\operatorname{Fun}(X_i,X_i)$. Restrict $\beta$, its inverse and both triangles to $Y_i\times\Delta^r$ in exactly the same way: their vertex functors are $fg$ and $\operatorname{id}_Y$, so all image vertices have label $i$. This gives an equivalence edge $f_ig_i\to\operatorname{id}_{Y_i}$. Clause (2) of [lem-coef-joyal-quasicategory-characterizations] now proves each $f_i$ is a categorical equivalence. Empty summands cause no restriction problem: a simplicial set with no vertices has no simplices, so all parameter maps with empty source are the unique empty maps. If $Y_i$ has a vertex, step 4 supplies a vertex in $X_i$; if $X_i$ has a vertex, $f_i$ supplies one in $Y_i$. Finally for $I=\varnothing$ both total objects are empty and the unique map is its own quasi-inverse with the unique (degenerate) equivalence witnesses. Thus the proof includes every stated empty case.

source.place: Agent-written restriction of the inverse edge and its triangle witnesses, followed by Corollary 3.6.6 and Theorem 3.6.8, printed pp.114-116.
